records.name: Krister
records.facts_used: In Scandinavian naming tradition Krister is a form of Kristian, alongside the spellings Christer and Crister. Its older basis is Latin Christianus and Greek Christianos, Christian. This family is distinct from the Kristofer family meaning Christ-bearer. A specific literary use is the character Krister in Tarjei Vesaas’s 1946 work Bleikeplassen. This is an example from Norwegian literature, not evidence for when the name entered Estonia. Estonian use is separately documented by the national name-statistics catalogue.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: The name scholar’s SNL article documents the Kristian/Christianus family and the Krister character in Vesaas’s 1946 Bleikeplassen. This is explicitly Norwegian literary history, not a first Estonian attestation. Statistics Estonia confirms independent exact-form use; no current population count is copied into narrative.

records.name: Kristo
records.facts_used: The Estonian dictionary entry connects Kristo with short forms of both Kristjan and Kristofer. These are distinct lines: Kristjan leads to Christianus, Christian, while Kristofer leads to a name meaning Christ-bearer. One route need not be assigned to every bearer. Tallinn University’s announcement of the 2013 laureates describes guitarist and teacher Kristo Käo. In 2007 he created an interactive guitar-learning portal. The announcement also connects his work with music-teacher training and bringing guitar playing into school lessons.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: The exact Estonian Wiktionary section gives both Kristjan and Kristofer. Behind the Name names only the Estonian Kristjan route and gives an Albanian Kristofor route; no Albanian martyr or Finnish literary evidence is reassigned to Estonia. Tallinn University’s 2013 announcement documents Käo’s 2007 portal.

records.name: Risto

records.name: Arkadijus
records.facts_used: Arkadijus is connected with Greek Arkadios, from Arcadia. Arcadia is a historical region of Greece, so the name’s basis is geographical. That meaning does not establish an Arcadian ancestry for every person who bears the name. Lithuania’s National Library announced the evening Aktorius be kaukės with Arkadijus Vinokuras for 12 June 2026. Its programme presented him as an actor and mime artist whose experience included Sweden’s Royal Dramatic Theatre and European circuses.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: The Greek Arkadios/Arcadia geographical explanation is documented by the opened guide. The national library’s announcement schedules an event for 12 June 2026; the text reports an announcement, not independently confirmed attendance.

records.name: Eirimė
records.facts_used: The Lithuanian guide explains Eirimė as a two-stem name: ei- is compared with eiti, to go, and rim- with rimti and ramintis, to grow calm. These are comparisons for individual elements, rather than a reason to invent one exact sentence translating the whole name. The name calendar in the 1964 Chicago publication Tikiu Dievą places Eirimė on 13 November with short form Eira. The list by A. Salys and priest Stasys Yla was reprinted in the second volume of Salys’s writings in 1983. This dates a publication, not the name’s invention.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: The guide supports the two-stem comparison, without an invented combined literal meaning. Salys PDF page 317, printed page 302, was visually checked for November 13 Eirimė (Eira). This is the 1964 calendar reprinted in 1983, not a coining date. The modern guide lists another day; the supplied national calendar remains unchanged.

records.name: Eugenijus
records.facts_used: Eugenijus is a Lithuanian form in a Greek-derived name family. The guide gives Greek eugenios; the wider family’s history is connected with eugenēs, well-born or noble. Different languages preserve the shared basis while developing their own endings and spellings. Poet and translator Eugenijus Ališanka graduated from Vilnius University’s Mathematics Faculty in 1983. The Lithuanian Writers’ Union bibliography dates his poetry collection Lygiadienis to 1991 and Peleno miestas to 1995.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: Greek eugenios/eugenēs family evidence is kept distinct from the modern poet’s biography. The Writers Union bibliography gives Lygiadienis 1991 and Peleno miestas 1995; these dates were checked rather than inferred from the English book title. The guide lists another day, which is not imported.

records.name: Norvydas
records.facts_used: Norvydas is a Lithuanian two-stem name. The guide compares nor- with noras and norėti, wish and to want, and vyd- with vydo, saw. These old name elements can be discussed separately without turning them into a promise or a description of someone’s character. Norvydas, with short form Noras, appears on 13 November in the 1964 Tikiu Dievą name calendar. This list by A. Salys and Stasys Yla was reprinted in Salys’s writings in 1983. It is a specific printed example of the name and its short form, rather than evidence of their year of creation.
records.reason: Opened references and an exact-form dictionary, historical publication, professional or cultural record support the reviewed account.
records.uncertainties: The guide’s nor-/vyd- comparisons remain element glosses, not a forced combined translation. Salys PDF page 317, printed page 302, visually confirms November 13 Norvydas (Noras) in the 1964 calendar reprinted in 1983.

records.name: Augenija
records.facts_used: The dictionary explicitly relates Augenija to Eiženija in the Greek eugenēs family, with the basic sense well-born or noble. The relationship rests on a dictionary cross-reference rather than an inference from the opening vowel alone. The family’s Latvian history is illustrated by masculine Eižens, recorded in Riga in 1869 and in the calendar in 1884. Those are dates for the related form. The Augenija entry supplies no comparable early dated attestation, so these years cannot be presented as its first records.
